title: Korea–Canada Strategic Energy & Industrial Partnership
subtitle: Where deeper industrial integration creates strategic value, through which instruments, and where to stay out
label: Generated from Allied Industrial Base Explorer data and a curated external evidence layer (accessed 2026-11-06); evidence, sources and caveats in the appendix. Data as of 30 October 2026.
disclosure: Rule-generated from the data (R/partnerships) with external facts from a dated, curated evidence layer; not yet checked by an independent verifier. Items marked partial or unverified must be confirmed before citation.

inlines.v: Permanent Magnets & Drive Systems: Electric Vehicles refining (joint). Nuclear Fuel & Reactor Systems: Uranium conversion & enrichment (Canada->Korea). Battery Materials & Cells: Accumulator parts & separators (Korea->Canada). Grid Equipment & Conductors: Solar refining (joint).

Recognise trusted partner supply of batteries extraction (cobalt ores, lithium minerals, natural graphite); accumulator parts & separators; oil extraction in procurement and content rules. Common anti-circumvention rules for electric vehicles refining (rare-earth metals, rare-earth oxides & compounds). Keep nuclear special materials; battery recycling feed; semiconductor manufacturing equipment open to global sourcing.
Upgrade Critical-minerals and energy-security MOU (2023) and 2026 stockpiling track: sector strategy, reciprocal commitments, a KPI dashboard and an annual review. No new MOU.

Do not co-subsidise new Batteries assembly (li-ion cells & packs, other accumulators) capacity. Do not create a new bilateral energy MOU or a free-standing MEA institution. Do not put new public money behind Cathode materials & precursors investment that is already committed (evidence KRCA-17.

Of 142 technology x stage cells and electro-industrial nodes assessed for the pair, 22 show an active complementarity (a supplier meeting the other's need, a shared chokepoint, a capacity-constrained trusted supplier or a chain specialisation), 1 direct competition and 94 no strategic case. The relationship is not one of general similarity: most of the electro-industrial base needs no bilateral intervention.

AIB strategic roles: Korea Specialized Technology & Manufacturing Anchor (primary), Scale Manufacturing & Integration Platform (primary), Coordination / Bridge Hub (secondary), Capital & Investment Anchor (secondary); Canada Resource & Processing Anchor (primary), Capital & Investment Anchor (secondary), Demand & Market Anchor (secondary).

Canada supplies uranium conversion & enrichment, nickel intermediates & chemicals, aluminium wire rod where Korea is short; Korea supplies accumulator parts & separators, cathode materials & precursors, non-oriented electrical steel (ngo), power cables where Canada is short; they share no node-level chokepoint where neither supplies.

From the AIB roles, Korea brings specialised technology and manufacturing, scale manufacturing, coordination across allied chains; Canada brings resources and processing, capital, demand and offtake. Public finance runs through KEXIM, K-SURE, KOMIR, KDB on the Korea side and ISED, EDC, CIB, CGF, CMIF, FinDev on the Canada side. The trade is market access and demand certainty for trusted capacity.

This section sets out what already exists before anything new is proposed. Facts are from the curated evidence layer (accessed 2026-11-06); items marked partial or unverified rest on secondary sources and should be confirmed before citation.
Canada's memberships in OSI's economic-security agreements table: G7, MSP, NATO, U.S. FTA.

Economic-security 2+2 (Joly, Champagne, Park Jin, Ahn Dukgeun) launched Sep 2022 and first met in Seoul on 16 May 2023; priorities were critical minerals, clean energy, supply chains, AI and economic coercion.

Second 2+2 (first was Nov 2024) agreed to pursue an update of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Action Plan, start Defence Cooperation Agreement steps and coordinate on economic security; the statement does not mention critical minerals or energy; next meeting in Korea in 2028.

On 2 Jun 2026 Canada and Korea agreed to develop a joint critical-minerals stockpiling plan by end-2026, discussed strategic-resource investments, and Korea agreed to facilitate CKFTA preferential tariffs for Canadian crude; no volumes or amounts given.

Lee and Carney agreed on 16 Jun 2026 to strengthen cooperation in defence, security, energy and critical minerals; an informal meeting followed at the NATO summit; no deliverables or amounts reported.
In the OSI energy basket, Korea imported US$3.7bn from Canada and Canada imported US$3.4bn from Korea (bilateral flows 2024, summed over the technology x stage cells).

Signed in Ottawa 22 Sep 2014 and in force 1 Jan 2015; Canada's first FTA in Asia-Pacific, covering goods, services, investment and procurement; nearly 90% of Canadian exports to Korea duty-free at entry into force.
From 26 Dec 2025 Canada cut FTA-partner steel quotas to 75% of 2024 volumes with a 50% over-quota surtax; Korea protested that this breaches the CKFTA and sought an exemption, none found.

The Comprehensive Strategic Partnership was launched in 2022 and is the base for the Jan 2026 industrial MOU; leaders agreed in Sep 2022 to develop a critical-minerals and energy MOU; day of launch inferred from the Sep 2022 summit.

Non-binding MOU (2023, not 2022) covering critical-mineral value chains, clean fuels and CCS, and clean-energy, ZEV and semiconductor manufacturing, with an action plan and investment-screening cooperation; it lets Korea count Canada toward the US EV-credit minerals test.

Carney and Lee welcomed the partnership at the Gyeongju APEC summit on 30 Oct 2025, Canada's first in the Indo-Pacific, and finalised a classified-information agreement that supports defence procurement; the readout does not mention energy, critical minerals or LNG.

Joly and Korea's Trade, Industry and Resources Minister Kim Jung-kwan signed in Ottawa; sets up an industrial cooperation committee and a forum on a Korean auto footprint, battery production, materials processing and critical-minerals recycling; no amounts or companies named.

The Geological Survey of Canada and Korea's KIGAM signed an implementation agreement on naturally occurring hydrogen research and development, announced with the 2 Jun 2026 energy and critical-minerals meeting.

Keep Korea exports of Nuclear components (fuel assemblies & zirconium, reactor parts) to Canada tariff-free and predictable; the buyer's need is met by the trusted supplier.
Keep Korea exports of Nuclear assembly (nuclear reactors & enrichment machinery) to Canada tariff-free and predictable; the buyer's need is met by the trusted supplier.
Common specifications for Solar refining (copper wire & rod, polysilicon) so a joint supplier base can serve both markets.
Recognise Korea output of Accumulator parts & separators as trusted domestic-equivalent supply in Canada procurement and content rules; capacity, not access, is the constraint.
Recognise Canada output of Oil extraction as trusted domestic-equivalent supply in Korea procurement and content rules; capacity, not access, is the constraint.
Keep Korea exports of Coal components to Canada tariff-free and predictable; the buyer's need is met by the trusted supplier.
Leave Nuclear special materials open to global sourcing: trusted supply is adequate and diversified, so a bilateral preference adds cost without security.
Leave Battery recycling feed open to global sourcing: trusted supply is adequate and diversified, so a bilateral preference adds cost without security.
Leave Semiconductor manufacturing equipment open to global sourcing: trusted supply is adequate and diversified, so a bilateral preference adds cost without security.
Leave Copper ores & concentrates open to global sourcing: trusted supply is adequate and diversified, so a bilateral preference adds cost without security.
Leave Lithium minerals open to global sourcing: trusted supply is adequate and diversified, so a bilateral preference adds cost without security.
Leave Silver powder open to global sourcing: trusted supply is adequate and diversified, so a bilateral preference adds cost without security.
No bilateral preference for Batteries assembly (li-ion cells & packs, other accumulators): both are strong suppliers; keep the market contestable.
